title: Jail for AI Prank: Crocodile Image Sparks Massive Operation in Singapore
key_facts: Singapore police arrested a man for posting an AI-made image of a crocodile in Pandan Reservoir.
On 20 Aug the national water agency received a report of a crocodile and launched a search; water activities were closed for two days.
The image was identified as made with Google's Gemini model.
The suspect, a 30-year-old Myanmar national, faces a fine and up to 10 years in prison on two charges: false information and obstructing justice.
He allegedly deleted the image and his request history; he plans to plead guilty; next hearing is in November.
quote_evidence: Emergency services spent two days searching for a non-existent reptile until specialists identified the hoax.
It turned out that the circulated image had nothing to do with reality and was created using the generative AI model Gemini.
why_it_matters_hint: One fake image triggered a real emergency response, now leading to criminal charges.
notes: hi-Tech.ua names no earlier outlet; the first reporter is not credited. Fine figure given as $7,800 in the article (currency unclear), omitted. Event from August, so score lowered by 1. Defendant's name left out.
